text:
monica: Need a compact battlecard snippet pack for SDRs + partners. Goal: three paste-ready headers (one line), three webinar openers (15-20s), two short rebuttals vs cloud-managed endpoints, and one demo CTA. Ship by EOD.

aj: OK. Quick framing idea: focus on predictability, operational controls, and cost levers. Avoid talking about models themselves.

sara: Draft one-liners (SDR-friendly):
- "Predictable inference — consistent latency and transparent unit economics for your LLM features."
- "Operational controls that matter — Dedicated, Private, and routing policies to keep SLAs intact."
- "Cost levers, not surprises — batching, KV caching, and quantization tuned to your workload."

ben: Webinar openers (short):
- "When customers ask why not just use a cloud endpoint, we say: those endpoints expose you to variable latency and hidden token costs. We optimize serving so your users see fast, stable experiences and your finance team sees predictable spend."
- "Small changes at the serving layer — like KV caching and smarter batching — can reduce redundant generations and cut your per-session cost materially. Today we'll show a live demo."
- "For regulated apps, Dedicated and Private deployments mean you get both performance and controls: private networking, audit logs, and SLA guarantees."

devon: Two rebuttals (very short) for SDRs to paste:
- Q: "Isn't this the same as cloud vendor X managed endpoints?"
  A: "No — Redwood adds serving-level optimizations (caching, batching, routing) and deployment tiers that give predictable p95/SLOs and lower unit costs."
- Q: "What about model parity when using quantized variants?"
  A: "We run evals on your prompt sets and surface per-profile regressions so rollouts are safe."

monica: Love the tone. Can we tighten language to be even shorter for Slack copy? Also add a one-line demo CTA: strong, action-oriented.

aj: Shortened one-liners:
- "Predictable latency and unit economics for LLM features."
- "Deployment controls: Dedicated, Private, regional routing."
- "Reduce cost with caching, batching, and per-workload quantization."

sara: Short webinar hooks (one sentence each):
- "We focus on serving, not model ownership — that means consistent p95 latency and fewer surprise bills."
- "Watch how KV caching and batching cut redundant tokens in a live chat demo."
- "Get enterprise-grade controls (VPC, KMS, audit logs) while keeping performance predictable."

ben: CTA: "Try a Redwood demo — see your app at p95 <200ms in 30 minutes. Schedule: <https://cal.redwood.ai/demo>"

devon: Add a tiny bench line for SDRs to use when asked for numbers: "Internal benchmark: p95 generation latency ~180-220ms on Dedicated SKU for mid-size chat models; comparable public endpoints often see 400-800ms under load (workload-dependent). See linked notes."

monica: Good. Final ask: include a single-line legal-safe shield for claims: "Benchmarks are workload-dependent; contact us for a tailored test." Drop everything into a one-pager and tag enablement.

aj: I'll paste this into the battlecard doc and tag enablement.

sara: +1. I'll add the short rebuttals into the objection-handling section.

ben: I'll prepare a concise PDF asset with headers, hooks, rebuttals, CTA, and the shield line.

devon: Draft uploaded to the marketing folder: <https://docs.redwood.ai/marketing/sdr-battle-pack-draft> — please review before EOD.

monica: Thanks team — if no major edits, enablement: please pull these lines into the SDR playbook before tomorrow's sync. :thumbsup:
